concepts.def: Oneness of Allah; foundational Islamic doctrine; Shahadah declares 'there is no god but Allah'; opposes shirk (idolatry).
Sunni beliefs: Allah, angels (malaikah), books (kutub), prophets (rasul), Last Day, predestination (al-qadr).
Shia beliefs: Tawhid, Adalat (justice), Nubuwwah (prophethood), Imamah (Imams), Mi'ad (resurrection).
Prophethood; 25 prophets named in Qur'an including Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, ending with Muhammad as Seal of Prophets.
Final revelation to Muhammad over 23 years through Angel Jibril; 114 chapters (surah); preserved unchanged in Arabic.
Afterlife; Day of Judgement (Yawm al-Din) when deeds weighed; Paradise (Jannah) or Hell (Jahannam) follow.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Islam: The Four Rightly Guided Caliphs — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Islam: The Four Rightly Guided Caliphs brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Islam: The Four Rightly Guided Caliphs.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Pilgrimage
Oneness of God

The Islamic declaration of faith: 'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah' — affirming monotheism and Muhammad's prophethood.
The Shahada is the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
The Shahada is the requirement to pray five times a day.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
The Shahada is the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.
Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.

mcqs.q: What does Buddhism teach about suffering?
options: Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
Buddhism teaches that life is nothing but pain and misery.
Buddhism teaches that suffering is caused by demons.
All existence involves dukkha (suffering/unsatisfactoriness), caused by tanha (craving and attachment); ending craving leads to liberation from suffering.
